verdict.rationale: gstack ships a large set of specialized 'skills' (review, QA, ship, debugging, design, autoplan/auto-review pipeline) that a user can delegate tasks to, with a router that sends any request to the right skill and skills that run autonomously to completion (e.g. auto-review runs CEO/design/eng/DX skills sequentially with auto-decisions). Community commentary corroborates the 'distinct specialist personas for planning, review, QA, shipping' pattern as a real, working feature. However, gstack itself is not a standalone AI model — it operates as an orchestration layer on top of external AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, etc.), so the 'built-in assistant' is really the host agent directed by gstack's skill files, not a self-contained assistant native to gstack. Missing for 10: evidence of a fully self-contained assistant independent of a host LLM agent, and independent hands-on verification that delegation/autonomous skill execution works reliably end-to-end.
